model: EE850D / EE820D duct CO2 transmitter (BACnet MS/TP)
applies_to: E+E EE850 CO2 / humidity / temperature duct transmitters and EE820 CO2 transmitters with the RS485 BACnet MS/TP output.
summary: The EE850D (CO2, humidity and temperature) and EE820D (CO2 only) are transmitters that work as BACnet MS/TP smart sensors. CO2 comes first in the object list (AI 0-1); the EE850D adds temperature, humidity and the calculated humidity values on AI 2-9.
notes: Object list from the PICS sections 11-12 (dated 03.07.2018). The EE820D has only AI 0 and AI 1.
The object order differs from the EE800D room transmitter: CO2 is AI 0 here.
The transmitter-difference table heads both columns EE850D; the second column (CO2 only) is the EE820D per the object list.
All objects are read-only except Present_Value while Out_Of_Service is true.

integration.summary: Set a unique device instance and MAC address, then poll AI 0 for CO2. On the EE850D also read temperature (AI 2) and humidity (AI 3).
setup: Device instance (0-4194302) and device name are writable and kept in non-volatile memory; the default name is the model plus 8 unique characters.
RS485 settings are one writable string property, default "9600-8n1"; baud 9600-115200, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit fixed.
Max Master is writable, up to 127.
ReinitializeDevice and DeviceCommunicationControl need the password printed in the PICS.
gotchas: Present_Value is only writable while Out_Of_Service is true; the value then defaults to 50.0.
Default RS485 string is 9600-8n1 here, not 38400 as on other E+E sensors.
